other_failure_modes.name: Inconsistent categorical encoding between train and test
other_failure_modes.description: Converting categorical columns to the Pandas 'category' dtype separately on train and test sets creates independent categorical mappings. If the unique values differ between the sets, the underlying integer codes representing the categories will misalign, causing tree-based models like LightGBM to misinterpret test features and produce completely incorrect predictions.

other_failure_modes.name: Unreported validation metrics
other_failure_modes.description: The agent implements cross-validation but fails to calculate or report any validation metric (e.g. RMSE) across the folds. While the model trains correctly, the lack of logged metrics prevents the user from assessing the model's offline performance before evaluating on the test set.

summary: The agent implements a solid cross-validation and ensembling framework using LightGBM and CatBoost, but falls short by lacking feature engineering and using a naive equal-weight ensemble. Critically, it introduces a severe data corruption bug by casting categorical columns to the Pandas 'category' dtype separately for the train and test sets, which will misalign the underlying integer codes used by LightGBM during inference.
